newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Two Singapore soldiers killed in NZ training.
newsitem.headline: Two Singapore soldiers killed in NZ training.

text.p: Two Singaporean soldiers were killed and 12 soldiers were injured on Sunday when an artillery shell exploded prematurely during a training exercise in New Zealand, an army spokesman said.
It was the second fatal accident in just over two weeks involving Singaporean soldiers at the central North Island army training base of Waiouru.
Eleven of the injured in Sunday's explosion were Singaporeans and one a New Zealander, who was slightly hurt.
"There was an accident at a Singapore gun position. The Singaporeans sustained 13 casualties including two fatalities," New Zealand army spokesman Major Steven French told Reuters.
"It would appear a shell exploded prematurely."
He said the injured were being ferried by four helicopters to nearby hospitals. Their injuries ranged from serious to light, French said, adding that he could give no more details.
In Singapore, meanwhile, the Defence Ministry said it would send a team of weapons experts to New Zealand on Sunday to investigate the deaths.
It said the weapon involved was a 155-mm field artillery gun.
"All live firing of this weapon system has been suspended until our team of experts has determined the exact causes of the accident," said Singapore's chief of army Major-General Han Eng Juan.
The ministry identified the two men killed as Third Sargeant Tan Han Chong, 21, an artillery specialist, and Lance Corporal Low Yin Tit, 18, a gunner.

The Singaporean soldiers, from the 23rd artillery battalion, arrived in New Zealand in early February and were due to return in April. The battalion was involved in a live-fire exercise at the time of the accident.
Singaporean soldiers regularly train in New Zealand because of the shortage of facilities and space in the city-state.
Last month, one Singaporean soldier was killed and another seriously injured after their Land Rover rolled and crashed in an accident at the Waiouru camp.
